Which screens you open, whether you upload by sharing or by picking files, roughly how many pages (1, 2–5 or 6+) and what kind of file, the app version, Android version, phone model and language. Never your server address, username, or anything about your documents: no titles, contents, tags, correspondents, file names or IDs. Sent to VKNXWorks\' own server, not to any analytics company.
Share anonymous usage stats so I can see which features people use and which Android versions to support.
You can change this any time in Settings.
Connect to your Paperless-ngx server with the address you\'d open in a browser.
Not encrypted (HTTP). Your password and documents are sent in the clear. Fine on your home network, risky anywhere else.
Not encrypted (HTTP). At home, your token and documents go to this address in the clear. PaperCtrl only switches to it when Paperless answers there.
PaperCtrl uses this address whenever it answers, which is faster at home, and the main address everywhere else. It switches by itself when your network changes.

Use a token if you sign in to Paperless with single sign-on (SSO), or if you\'d rather not enter your password here. In the Paperless web app, open your profile picture → My Profile, and copy or generate the API Auth Token.
PaperCtrl only stores an API token, encrypted on this phone, and only sends it to your server. Your password is used once to get the token and is never saved.

PaperCtrl couldn\'t connect to this server over HTTPS. It can try plain HTTP instead, but then your password and documents are sent unencrypted and anyone on the network can read them. Only do this on a network you trust.

Signing in worked, but the home-network address couldn't be checked:

%1$s

You can save the server without it now and add it again later.
%1$s presented a certificate that Android doesn\'t trust. That\'s normal for a self-signed certificate on your own server. Check that the fingerprint below matches your server\'s before you trust it.

%1$s presented a different certificate from the one you trusted before. If you didn\'t renew or replace it yourself, someone may be intercepting the connection. Only continue if the fingerprint below matches your server\'s new certificate.
On the server, this command prints it: openssl x509 -noout -fingerprint -sha256 -in your-cert.pem
Tap a server to switch to it.
PaperCtrl forgets the server and its token, and deletes anything still waiting in the upload queue for it. The token stays valid on the server; you can delete it there from your profile.
Couldn\'t reach the server. Check the address, and that your phone can reach it (Wi-Fi, VPN).
The secure connection failed, so nothing was sent. The server\'s certificate wasn\'t accepted.
The server\'s certificate has changed since you trusted it. Remove the server and add it again to check the new one.
The server didn\'t accept the token. It may have been deleted or replaced; sign in again.
This account uses two-factor authentication. Enter the code from your authenticator app.
That authentication code wasn\'t right. Codes change every 30 seconds; try the current one.
Something answered at this address, but not Paperless-ngx\'s API. Check the address; if Paperless runs under a sub-path, include it (for example example.com/paperless).

The address forwards to a sign-in page on %1$s instead of to Paperless. If your reverse proxy protects Paperless with a login (Authelia, Authentik…), let the /api/ path through without it, or use the home-network address.
This Paperless-ngx version is too old for PaperCtrl. Update the server to a current version.
This server runs Paperless-ngx %1$s, which is too old for PaperCtrl. Update it to a current version.
Your account isn\'t allowed to do this on the server.
It\'s no longer on the server.
Too many attempts. Wait a minute and try again.
The server ran into a problem. Check its logs.
Blocked an unencrypted (HTTP) connection the server redirected to.
The file is too large for the server. If Paperless runs behind a reverse proxy, raise its upload limit (client_max_body_size in Nginx).
Anything left on Automatic is filled in by Paperless\' own matching after it reads the document.
Couldn\'t load your tags and correspondents
Documents you scan or share to PaperCtrl wait here until Paperless has them, even without a connection.
Waiting for the server to be reachable
Paperless is still processing it; checking again shortly
The file is no longer on this phone. Remove this item and share or scan it again.
The server this was meant for was removed from PaperCtrl.
The file is deleted from this phone and won\'t be uploaded.
Paperless already has the file and may still add it. PaperCtrl stops following it and deletes its copy on this phone.
Handy for the pages of one letter. Turn it off to upload each image as its own document.
Leave anything you don\'t know on Automatic
Couldn\'t prepare the files for upload.
Open PaperCtrl and connect to your Paperless-ngx server first, then share again.
PaperCtrl couldn\'t read what was shared, or it\'s larger than 1 GB. Try sharing the file itself rather than a link to it.
Shows progress while documents upload and Paperless processes them.
